title: Gran Torino
about: A grumpy Korean War veteran in Detroit stops the Hmong boy next door stealing his 1972 Gran Torino, and slowly becomes family.
cue: Serve the skewers when Sue brings Walt to the barbecue next door.

    To StartGrilled Hmong pork sausage with chilli dipWalt is out of beer. Lemongrass pork sausage and fiery jeow.How to make it600g pork mince, not too lean2 lemongrass stalks, white part finely chopped4 garlic cloves, crushed2 spring onions, finely sliced1 tbsp fish sauce1 tsp chilli flakes3 long red chillies2 limes1/2 cup coriander, choppedMix the pork with the lemongrass, half the garlic, spring onion, fish sauce, chilli flakes and a little salt.Shape into thick logs on skewers and chill while the grill heats.Char the whole chillies on the grill, then pound them with the rest of the garlic, lime juice, coriander and salt into a dip.Grill the sausages, turning, until browned and cooked through, then slice and serve with the dip.Pounded green papaya saladNo touching heads at the barbecue. Shredded papaya pounded with chilli and lime.How to make it1 green papaya, peeled and shredded2 garlic cloves2 small red chillies1 tbsp palm sugar2 tbsp fish sauce2 limes, juiced8 cherry tomatoes, halved100g snake beans, cut short30g roasted peanuts, crushedPound the garlic, chillies and palm sugar in a mortar.Add the beans and tomatoes and bruise them lightly.Add the papaya, fish sauce and lime juice and pound and toss until it softens a little.Pile onto a plate and scatter with peanuts.Prawn crackers by the bowlfulIt's not Toad, it's Thao.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsLemongrass chicken skewers with sticky riceFood piles up on Walt's porch. Charred chicken with herbs and lime.How to make it800g chicken thigh fillets, cut in strips2 lemongrass stalks, finely chopped3 garlic cloves, crushed2 tbsp fish sauce1 tbsp brown sugar1 tbsp vegetable oil400g glutinous rice, soaked overnight1 cup mint and coriander leaves2 limes12 bamboo skewers, soakedSteam the drained rice in a lined steamer until tender and sticky.Mix the lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce, sugar and oil and toss the chicken through.Thread onto skewers and grill over high heat, turning, until charred and cooked through.Serve with the sticky rice, herbs and lime wedges.Kowalski's kielbasa and krautWalt is a retired Ford factory man. Smoked kielbasa and buttery kraut.How to make it800g smoked kielbasa sausage1 brown onion, sliced30g butter500g jar sauerkraut, drained1 tsp caraway seeds4 crusty rye rolls4 tbsp hot mustardCook the onion slowly in the butter, then add the sauerkraut and caraway and warm through.Score the kielbasa and grill, turning, until blistered and hot through.Serve on the rolls with the kraut and mustard.Something SweetCoconut tapioca with pandan jellyWalt leaves the Gran Torino to Thao. Chilled coconut milk and green pandan jelly.How to make it80g small tapioca pearls2 tsp agar agar powder500ml water1 tsp pandan extract100g caster sugar400ml tin coconut milk1 pinch salt2 cups crushed iceBoil the tapioca in plenty of water until clear, then rinse in cold water.Boil the water with the agar, half the sugar and the pandan, pour into a tray and chill until set, then cut into strips.Warm the coconut milk with the rest of the sugar and the salt until dissolved, then chill.Spoon tapioca and jelly into glasses, add ice and pour over the coconut milk.To DrinkPabst Blue Ribbon on the porchWalt's empties stack up on the porch. Ice-cold cans and a folding chair.How to make it8 x 355ml cans of Pabst Blue Ribbon beer2 bags of iceBury the cans in ice.Hand them out and stack the empties.Hot jasmine teaFor anyone not on Walt's beer.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
